_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY -- not a real signature. Mirrors eval/fixtures/gate0_signature.example.json's shape for the APP-SERVER launch surface (tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py replacing tools/run_gate0_codex.ps1's -PaidExec path). IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM THE ORIGINAL: tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py does NOT itself implement a Confirm-PaidExecSignature-equivalent mechanical gate that reads this file -- it refuses to launch un-priced only via --credit-rate-pin (tools/gate0_codex_credit_rate.py::load_credit_rate_pin), exactly like tools/gate0_appserver_launch.py already does. This file is prepared as the SAME kind of human-authored authorization record David reviews/signs before a real launch (frozen_commit + the 20 PIN_FIELDS-adjacent launch-time hashes + the credit-rate pin), but its consumption is currently a MANUAL orchestrator discipline, not code-enforced the way the .ps1's signature check is. Flagged explicitly in reports/2026-07-24-gate0-prereg-amendment-appserver.md as a known gap versus the original mechanism -- a future PR could wire an equivalent Confirm-PaidExecSignature check into tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py if that mechanical enforcement is wanted.
expected_config_sha256: PENDING_RECOMPUTE_AT_LAUNCH -- this launch's freshly computed handshake-receipt.json:config_sha256 (tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::render_full_config_toml output, hashed at signature time)
expected_codex_mcp_list_sha256: PENDING_RECOMPUTE_AT_LAUNCH -- this launch's freshly computed handshake-receipt.json:codex_mcp_list_sha256 (tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::codex_mcp_list_json output, hashed at signature time)
_comment_launcher_hash: The launcher whose identity this pins is the NEW arm runner, tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py -- NOT tools/run_gate0_codex.ps1 (that file is unedited and unrelated to this launch surface). Same canonical git-blob-at-HEAD contract as the original (git -C <repo> diff --quiet HEAD -- tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py && git -C <repo> cat-file blob HEAD:tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py | sha256sum).
_comment_safety_critical_hashes: Same four safety-critical files as the original signature template -- tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py IMPORTS these unmodified (never edits them); pinning their hashes here still guards against a dirty/tampered working tree at launch time, exactly as the original mechanism intends.
_comment_appserver_launch_sha256: ADDITIONAL pin versus the original template -- tools/gate0_appserver_launch.py (the M1-proven client wiring tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py imports: ObservingGate0Client, LiveCreditGuard, AppServerUsageTracker, build_overrides, ...) is just as safety-relevant on this transport as the four files above.

credit_rate_pin._comment: Identical contract to the original template (PR #118 checklist 4a) -- tools/gate0_codex_credit_rate.py::load_credit_rate_pin refuses an empty rate_source or a model mismatch, unchanged by transport.
